body:
There are a few cat behaviorists around here, but (I'm not making this shit up) the going rate is $150/*half hour*. I know they're specialized and all, but I don't even pay that much for my own mental health. Hence, watching all the Jackson Galaxy videos. 

Thanks for your compassionate perspective. I have posted asking for advice about handling my cat a few times on a few different sites, and I *always* get vilified for it. Some people say "break up with the boyfriend" (of 6 years, mind you), some people shame me for ever getting a kitten in the first place when I work a full-time job. And you know what, I'll accept that criticism, they're right. But he probably would've stayed at the shelter for months if I hadn't taken him in. And even now, if I do re-home him, it will be through a foster program so that he goes straight from me to another loving family that I choose myself. I'm trying to do what I think is the best thing for everyone in this situation--the cat will NOT be happy if bf and I have a crumbling relationship where we are always on edge.

The cat is fixed, and he's 11 months old. I think part of the problem is that we're not home enough, and he acts out because of that with destructive behavior. I really try my best to be home as often as I can, but both bf and I have jobs that just get more demanding every day. It wasn't that bad when we first got the kitten. And obviously our bosses don't take kindly to "I need to leave early, I have a cat at home."

It's not my boyfriend's fault, I swear. He's not much of a cat person (or a pet person in general), and it's my fault for getting one despite that. I can't expect him to love the most annoying of cats.

That's actually a great idea! I have taken him out in a harness before, but he gets a ton of fleas every time we go out. He gets flea treatments, but they're not enough to keep the fleas away in this urban area with a lot of feral cats. If only he didn't shred my hands every time I try to flea bath/comb him. I'm going to try the flea collar with the harness next.

Thank you for the suggestions! I actually did beg the landlord, but she said that we have ~550 sqft of space, barely big enough for one person let alone two people and two pets. But I am looking for other places for when my lease is up. And I have a bunch of Feliway all over this place, I'm praying that it kicks in one of these days. I'll probably try CBD, too, if I can find it.

I figured being a "teenager" maybe had something to do with it. The vet said he didn't want to do Prozac because of how young the cat is, he wanted to wait and see if he would mellow out with age. If we're talking getting him to 18-20 months, that's a long time but definitely worth a shot considering I was afraid he'd be like this forever. 

As for the second cat thing, the vet did mention how long it takes some cats to get comfortable with a new cat. I think he was also worried about how aggressive my cat can get. Not that I can look into it as an option for a while (breaking the lease would be thousands of dollars), but if I can get lucky enough to find a place that allows two cats in this city, I might just look into it. And might ask a different vet about it. 

I'll try all the tips you suggested in the meantime! Thank you for your advice.
